answer: One defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a vote or claim a reward. A crystal-clear rule can slash the bond when an identity repeats a signed message or violates a challenge, while honest agents recover it after a delay. The trellis of linked attestations helps detect coordinated accounts, but the bond is the costly gate: an attacker must lock real capital in every Sybil identity and risks losing it, rather than minting identities for free. An atlas of reputation can help prioritize scrutiny, but should not replace the verifiable bond.
